_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE HOOKS' OWN GATE IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- \
.githooks/injection-sweep.json
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/git_hooks_smoke.rs` drives the REAL hook files
and the REAL side-workspace lister over throwaway repositories, which is
what makes them injectable at all: the subject is a shell script and the
oracle is a Rust suite. Every injection below removes one distinction those
scripts draw and names the case that must go red for it.
THE FIRST FOUR ARE ABOUT THE SAME DECISION, the one R1078 paid for and
R1127 to R1129 found unread in three gates: exit 1 says THESE SITES BREAK
THE LAW and exit 2 says I COULD NOT READ ENOUGH OF THIS TREE TO HAVE AN
OPINION. The gates answer both. Until R1132 nothing checked that their
callers told the two apart, and one of the four collapses is a tree the gate
never read being COMMITTED.
THE LAST FOUR ARE R1136's HALF OF THE CI REPORT. The hook used to READ
GitHub's answer itself, with three `gh -q` expressions no test here could
execute — measured silent twice, at 14 passed / 0 failed each time, while a
real `gh` would have reported a RED commit as clean. The reading is now
`tools/ci-state`, with its own sweep; what is left to this hook is CARRIAGE,
and carriage fails in ways of its own: asking about the wrong commit,
swallowing the answer, or passing over a reporter that could not answer.
THE LAST TWO ARE R1182's ARM, and they are here because the round that added
it did not add them. `check-side-workspaces.sh` grew a THIRD gate under the
same three-code contract, printing the same pair of sentences for exit 1 and
exit 2 — and both arms exit 1, so the sentence is the only thing that tells
them apart. Nothing read either one.
Scoped to the hook suite: nothing here touches a gate's own laws, which
have their own sweeps under tools/.
THE SUITE IS A MODULE OF `all` AND NOT A TARGET. R1171 folded seventy-six of
the cli crate's test files into one binary, this one among them, and a
`--test git_hooks_smoke` after that commit is `error: no test target named`
— which takes the eight injections below with it, since the harness refuses a
sweep whose control reached nothing. Measured on the tree that found it: the
control ran 0 targets. The trailing filter reproduces exactly the population
this command had before the fold.

injections.name: the-hook-reports-an-unreadable-tree-as-a-blind-wait
injections.why: the collapse the hook's own comment says it already made once: a workspace the gate could not read was reported as a wait on a clock, which sends somebody hunting for a `sleep` in a tree that has none

injections.name: the-hook-commits-a-tree-the-gate-could-not-read
injections.why: the other direction, and the dangerous one: a gate with no verdict is not a gate with nothing to say. Treating exit 2 as a pass commits a tree part of which was never read, which is the shape R1078 shipped

injections.name: the-lister-reports-an-unreadable-workspace-as-a-blind-wait
injections.why: the same collapse one level down, where it costs more: this message NAMES THE WORKSPACE, so the wrong sentence sends a reader into whichever crate the gate merely failed to read

injections.name: the-lister-cannot-say-it-was-never-started-in-a-tree
injections.why: the lister's OWN two codes, which nothing in this repository reads — the hook and CI both treat any non-zero as a rejection. A distinction with no reader drifts, so the suite is the reader: `2` is 'I was not started in a tree' and `1` is 'a workspace here failed its gate'

edits.from:
"tree to check, which is where a git hook and CI both start" >&2
  exit 2
edits.to:
"tree to check, which is where a git hook and CI both start" >&2
  exit 1

injections.name: the-hook-reports-on-whatever-commit-is-checked-out
injections.why: R1136. The reporter is asked about a commit and answers about THAT commit; hand it the working tree's HEAD instead of the published `origin/main` and every sentence it prints is true about the wrong subject — including, on the push that is fixing a red CI, a clean report about the commit being pushed. R1122 paid for this shape one gate over: format perfect, subject wrong

injections.name: the-hook-swallows-what-the-reporter-said
injections.why: the R890 blindness rebuilt one layer up. Four consecutive red runs went unnoticed for eleven hours because nothing here could SEE a red CI; a hook that runs the reporter and drops its output is that same silence, and it is worse, because the gate now looks like it is being run

injections.name: the-hook-passes-over-a-reporter-that-could-not-report
injections.why: the reporter exits 2 only when it could not produce a report AT ALL, and this hook is its one production reader. Ignoring that code makes a push where nothing was checked look exactly like a push where CI was checked and found fine — the collapse the first four injections here are about, arriving through a different door

injections.name: the-reporter-may-rewrite-the-lockfile-it-was-run-with
injections.why: R1115 measured that a cargo command allowed to resolve freely REWRITES a lockfile it disagrees with. A hook that drops `--locked` here edits a tracked file of this repository as a side effect of reporting on CI, and the edit lands in whatever the next commit stages

injections.name: the-lister-reports-an-unreadable-environment-as-one-left-to-the-machine
injections.why: the R1132 collapse arriving through the door R1182 opened. The environment gate answers 2 for a tree it could not read, and folding that into the finding arm tells somebody a test of theirs leaves a variable to the machine when the gate never got far enough to find one — sending them into a workspace to look for a defect nobody has claimed exists

injections.name: the-lister-passes-a-workspace-the-environment-gate-could-not-read
injections.why: the other direction and the dangerous one, the shape R1078 shipped: a gate with no verdict is not a gate with nothing to say. Keeping the sentence and dropping the rejection commits a workspace part of which was never read, and it is the exit code alone that catches it — the words on the screen are still perfectly true

      exit 1

injections.name: the-lister-reports-an-unreadable-workspace-as-a-bad-citation
injections.why: the collapse this arm SHIPPED with, and the only one of the three that was measured in the wild rather than reasoned about: a concurrent prune of the one shared build directory left `librocksdb-sys` uncompilable, the gate answered 2 and said so, and the lister printed `bench carries a citation that names no item` — sending a reader to hunt a citation that does not exist

injections.name: the-lister-passes-a-workspace-the-citation-gate-could-not-read
injections.why: the other direction, the one that commits a tree part of which was never read. The sentence stays true and only the rejection goes, so the exit code is the whole of what catches it
